chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: Staying in New York: Savoy Ballroom, Moe Gale and Chick Webb
summary: He played Roseland and the Savoy from 1935, where Moe Gale became his manager and he became house band after Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You didn't do much touring during that year. I mean, with the band 1935.
No. I was in, most of the time, I was in New York like the Ubangi Club and the theaters, and we did a lot of club
affairs like hotels. You know, I went down to Roseland Ballroom and played a week. And then, the Savoy came in in '35.

The Savoy was owned by the Gales, Moe Gale. I went up there to play a week, and then he turned out to be my personal manager. That's the reason I stayed in the Savoy so many years. When I got tired of travelling on the road, I'd go and I'd stay like 6 months, 7 months.

Like I said, well, I was alternating with Chick Webb. Chick Webb was the first band, and then I went in and alternated with him. And after Chick went out, then I was rated the house band up until the time they closed it down.
